title: Native Weil calculation on a compatible proper/open tower
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the native derived categories $D(\mathcal W_S)$, bounded constructible full subcategories $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(S)$, and equivariant operations of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Suppose given finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $V,U,\overline V,W,\overline W,T$ and $k_0$-maps
$$s:V\hookrightarrow U,\quad t:U\hookrightarrow\overline V,\quad i:W\hookrightarrow\overline W,\quad p:\overline V\to\overline W,\quad p_W:U\to W,\quad q:\overline W\to T,$$
where $s,t,i$ are quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] and $p,p_W,q$ are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume $pt=ip_W$ is Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $a=p_Ws$, $b=qi$ and $z=ts$, so $pz=ia$ and $qpz=ba$. For any compactification $c=(j,r)$, meaning a quasi-compact open followed by a proper map [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], write $F_c=Rr_*J_j$ with $J_j$ the termwise native extension by zero. Then $J_s$ carries $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)$ into $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(U)$, and there is a natural isomorphism of functors $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)\to D(\mathcal W_T)$ with the following intermediate derived identifications:
$$F_{(z,qp)}=R(qp)_*J_z\cong Rq_*Rp_*J_tJ_s\cong Rq_*J_iRp_{W*}J_s=F_{(i,q)}F_{(s,p_W)}.$$
The middle identification is the native proper/open isomorphism for $pt=ip_W$, evaluated only on $J_sK$ for bounded constructible $K$; the outer identification is the direct-image and open-extension composition identification. Every displayed isomorphism and its inverse is in the native equivariant derived category. No separatedness of the schemes over $k_0$ and no assertion on arbitrary unbounded inputs is imposed.

proof.text: Use the existing native derived functors in the statement. The open-composition instances make J_(ts) well typed. The Cartesian square supplies the equality t ≫ p = p_W ≫ i by IsPullback.w. No separate construction of a compactification is needed: all endpoints are already the explicit open-extension/direct-image functor composites. In particular the calculation need not invoke proper composition or prove additional geometric conclusions.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition, first four displayed equalities; agent adaptation using the cited native Weil statements.

proof.text: Apply part (b) of [lem-sf-native-weil-basic-comparisons] to the quasi-compact open $s:V\to U$. For every $K\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)$ it gives $L=J_sK\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(U)$. Consequently the restriction of $J_s$ has precisely the source and target required for the proper/open comparison in the next steps. This uses the native locally finite coefficient constructibility in that node. In Lean, let I be the inclusion of WC^der(V) into D(W_V), and lift I ⋙ J_s to WC^der(U) using ObjectProperty.lift and this preservation assertion. Composing that lift with the inclusion into D(W_U) is definitionally I ⋙ J_s.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition, first four displayed equalities; agent adaptation using the cited native Weil statements.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha:R(qp)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*Rp_*$ for part (a) of [lem-sf-native-weil-basic-comparisons], with $u=p$ and $v=q$, and write $\beta:J_tJ_s\xrightarrow{\sim}J_z$ for part (b), with $j=s$ and $i=t$. The first displayed identification at $K$ is the composite
$$R(qp)_*J_zK\xrightarrow{\alpha_{J_zK}}Rq_*Rp_*J_zK\xrightarrow{Rq_*Rp_*(\beta_K^{-1})}Rq_*Rp_*J_tJ_sK.$$
The direct-image comparison is available on the entire native derived category, so it requires no boundedness claim for $J_zK$ or any intermediate direct image. The open-composition comparison is also a native derived natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition, first four displayed equalities; agent adaptation using the cited native Weil statements.

proof.text:
In [lem-sf-native-weil-open-proper-interchange], substitute $U'=U$, $X'=\overline V$, $U=W$, $X=\overline W$, $j'=t$, $j=i$, and $p'=p_W$. Its commutativity hypothesis is exactly $pt=ip_W$; both vertical maps are proper, both horizontal maps are quasi-compact open, and all four schemes are of finite type over $k_0$. It supplies $\gamma:J_iRp_{W*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*J_t$ on $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(U)$. For the object $L=J_sK$ from step 2, apply the functor $Rq_*$ to $\gamma_L^{-1}$. This gives precisely
$$Rq_*Rp_*J_tJ_sK\xrightarrow{Rq_*(\gamma_{J_sK}^{-1})}Rq_*J_iRp_{W*}J_sK.$$
Only $J_sK$ is used as an input to the bounded-constructible interchange theorem. The Cartesian assumption of the item in particular gives the commutative square required there. Whisker the inverse of gamma on the left by that lifted functor and on the right by Rq_*; the inclusion/lift composite reduces definitionally to I ⋙ J_s.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition, first four displayed equalities; agent adaptation using the cited native Weil statements.

proof.text: By the definition $F_{(j,r)}=Rr_*J_j$ in the statement, the initial and final expressions of steps 3 and 4 are $F_{(z,qp)}K$ and $F_{(i,q)}F_{(s,p_W)}K$. Compose those two isomorphisms. For a morphism $u:K\to K'$, naturality of $\alpha,\beta$ and $\gamma$ gives the commutative squares for their evaluations at $K,K'$ and $J_sK,J_sK'$; applying $Rp_*$ and $Rq_*$ preserves the squares, and pasting gives the naturality square for the composite. Its inverse is obtained by reversing the arrows and replacing each comparison by its inverse. Each comparison and inverse already lies in the native equivariant derived category, and functors preserve inverses and composition. Hence the resulting isomorphism and its inverse are native equivariant morphisms, as asserted.
